1372	depends on which medications. First we'll address a patient who is
1373	in danger: these medications he must take, because if
1374	he doesn't take them his life is in danger, no question here.
1375	Even outright chametz he should take, because saving a life overrides
1376	the whole Torah, unless he can get an alternative. You can
1377	ask the doctor whether there are alternative medications kosher for Pesach.
1378	Almost every medication has
1379	a kosher-for-Pesach alternative, but if there isn't one, or the second one is
1380	not as good in quality, then it's a danger to life, so
1381	he should not endanger his life, and he is permitted to take any medication
1382	even if it is chametz. But when it's a patient who is not
1383	in danger, not a matter of danger to life, but he doesn't
1384	feel well, it depends on whether this medication has a good taste,
1385	like pills that are swallowed, not ones you would try to suck on,
1386	whose taste is not pleasant: it is permitted to take them on Pesach even
1387	if they are chametz. Why? Because he doesn't feel the taste.
1388	They have no taste, he swallows them. If there are alternative
1389	medications, then certainly he shouldn't take chametz, he should ask the doctor,
